discoveries:
- `gov skilleval`'s `--json` carries no reply text (W2-104 by design), so the interface's "summary of the reply as `--json` returned it" could not be met as worded. I captured replies with a pass-through shim instead.
- The harness copies every file of a skill folder except `scenarios.md` and the record into the session. Check 1 raised this as F2 (out of scope, fails open): see P-W2-100-F2 below.
- The copies ACT will also put `scenarios.md`, the records and the summaries into `.claude/skills/<skill>/`. Engineers loading the skill can read its scenarios; this does not affect the guard.
- The launcher's RUBRIC-2 moved product-spec and the test designer to Sonnet at C2; the auditors kept Opus.
- Ids the ticket could cite (not added to `Implements:`): DEC-802 (fixes ride along in the same round), DEC-1010 (review convergence), DEC-968 (the scoped run).
risks:
- Backend and security each have one clean 3/3 run at their current version. Backend scenario 3 passed only on the letter of its pass line (check 2's N3).
- W2-101 (domain skills B, in parallel) probably uses the same summaries form, so it would hit the same harness exposure (F2).
- Check 2's N2: fix 4 changed 1.0.2's text without a new version number. No run or record existed at 1.0.2 before it.
lessons:
- Move evaluation artefacts out of a skill folder before a skill is evaluated (until P-W2-100-F2 lands).
- Check any fix written from a judge's reason for the scenario's own nouns before any run.
- An interface reading should never pin a first version that the template says rises when the text changes.
proposed_decisions:
- **P-W2-100-CITP: the owner's yes on the kernel bytes (CAP-33).** Read `docs/changes/W2-100-CIT-P.md` (status PROPOSED, `owner_approval: 'pending'`; product head `f7637bd03e25`, branch head `cdac25763613`).
  - Options:
    - (a) Approve: the approval line is written into the CIT-P, the queue lands W2-100, and the copies ACT writes `.claude/skills/{backend,api,data,security}/`, which turns the 12 reds green. Cost: one approval line, then the ACT.
    - (b) Defer: engineers keep working without domain skills, and W2-101 has no landed sibling. Cost: nothing now.
    - (c) Re-baseline: fold the four into one skill, or move to option (b) of P-W2-100-IF-1. Cost: an engineer pair on three shipped modules, 1–2 days.
  - Recommendation (a), confidence high. It blocks this ticket's landing and the copies ACT.
- **P-W2-100-F2 (out of scope; fails open, P1 under the rubric):** `gov skilleval` copies `scenario-summaries.md` into the session (`src/gov/skilleval/harness.py:167-168`), so a weakened later version of a skill could pass on earlier replies.
  - Options:
    - (a) Add `scenario-summaries.md` to the harness's ignore list, with a test. About 1 h for a pair in its own ticket, which needs the owner's P1 (no new ticket without the owner).
    - (b) Move the summaries out of the skill folders. This changes this ticket's interface and W2-101's.
    - (c) Record the gap.
  - Recommendation (a), confidence high. It blocks nothing in W2-100, but it is an entry criterion for the next `gov skilleval` of any folder with a summaries file, including W2-101's (DEC-803).

recommended_next_action: Put P-W2-100-CITP to the owner. On the yes, write `owner_approval` and land the branch at `cdac25763613` (or its successor with the approval line), then queue the copies ACT. Take P-W2-100-F2 to the owner before W2-101's skilleval runs.
